topic: The Mystery of 'Both': Understanding Superposition and Quantum States
target_audience: High school students and science enthusiasts

sections.title: The Binary Boundary: A Classical Refresher
lecture_lines: Our daily world is built on binary choices.
A light switch is either fully ON or OFF.
In classical logic, there is no middle ground.
animations: Create a rectangular light switch with a toggle circle; toggle it from top (ON) to bottom (OFF).
Add labels '1' at the top and '0' at the bottom using a white (#FFFFFF) sans-serif font.
Fade in a large 'OR' (#AAAAAA) between the 1 and 0 to emphasize the classical choice.

sections.title: The Quantum Leap: What is Superposition?
lecture_lines: Quantum objects exist in multiple states at once.
Superposition is a fundamental state of being.
Imagine a coin lying flat as heads or tails.
Now, visualize that coin spinning rapidly on a table.
While spinning, it represents both states simultaneously.
animations: Display a 2D circle labeled 'H' (Heads) in blue (#0000FF).
Flip it to show 'T' (Tails) in red (#FF0000).
Simulate a spin by rapidly oscillating the circle's X-scale between 1 and 0.1.
While spinning, change the circle's color to a magenta (#FF00FF) blend of blue and red.
Add a glowing white (#FFFFFF) halo around the spinning coin to represent the superposition state.

sections.title: Mapping the State: The Bloch Sphere
lecture_lines: We map quantum states onto a sphere's surface.
The North Pole represents state zero or heads.
The South Pole represents state one or tails.
Every surface point is a valid quantum address.
The equator represents a perfect fifty-fifty superposition.
animations: Create a large white (#FFFFFF) circle with a dashed horizontal ellipse to suggest a 3D sphere.
Label the top point |0> and the bottom point |1> in white (#FFFFFF).
Add a yellow (#FFFF00) vector starting from the center pointing straight up to |0>.
Rotate the yellow vector 90 degrees to point towards the equator.
Draw a small, glowing point (#00FFFF) on the sphere's surface moving along the equator to show flexibility.

sections.title: The Act of Observation: Collapsing the Wave
lecture_lines: Observation forces a quantum system to choose.
This is called collapsing the wave function.
Imagine a box with a sleeping and awake cat.
Until measured, the cat exists in both states.
Looking inside forces reality into one single outcome.
animations: Draw two semi-transparent icons: a sleeping cat (#AAAAAA) and an awake cat (#FFFFFF) overlapping.
Introduce a cyan (#00FFFF) Eye symbol that glides from the right side towards the cats.
Remove the sleeping cat icon and make the awake cat icon 100% opaque instantly.

sections.title: Why It Matters: Parallel Processing Power
lecture_lines: Classical computers solve problems one step at a time.
Quantum bits explore all paths in a single moment.
Parallelism allows for massive jumps in processing power.
animations: Draw a simple 2D maze grid (#FFFFFF) with a red dot (#FF0000) exploring one path.
Reset the red dot to start and make it hit a different wall.
Spawn a cloud of 10 green dots (#00FF00) at the entrance.
Animate the 10 green dots moving simultaneously through different maze branches.
Highlight the successful path with a thick, glowing green line (#00FF00).
